title: Opus5.6 Suspected to Appear in Claude API; User Tests Find Training Data Updated to May 2026

content_html:
According to a MindStudio report, a user recently claimed on social platform X that they obtained replies from a new, unreleased Anthropic model through the normal Claude interface. The models in question have been informally called Opus 5.6 and Sonnet 5.6. However, Anthropic has not publicly confirmed this, and whether the models actually exist remains to be verified.

Currently, the related rumors are mainly based on two signals: first, some demos show that the models perform better than Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 in 3D scene generation and code generation; second, users tested the knowledge cutoff date and found that the models may have been trained on more recent data. The specific method is to disable web search and tool calls, then ask the model about verifiable events that occurred after its training cutoff date. User Cheddar Lua said that the model once mentioned information from May 2026 in a conversation.

In terms of performance testing, Opus 5.6 is said to have improved in proportional coordination, lighting, and the handling of physical relationships between objects in 3D scenes, but it still has difficulty building the geometric structure of a car from scratch. Opinions on the related claims are divided. Commentator Matt Berman publicly denied them, while some accounts said they had independently reproduced the relevant test signals.

Axios previously reported that Anthropic is internally developing more capable models, but the company has not officially confirmed the official name, release date, or pricing of Opus 5.6. This rumor also reflects continued outside attention to the progress of Anthropic's next-generation models, but the relevant performance information still lacks official verification.
